gap: No result ChatGPT got states that RTINGS, the only lab with a test of any candidate, found the Royal Kludge RK61's 1,000 Hz polling held to an effective 250 Hz update rate with latency it calls "high and inconsistent", on a unit that connects by Bluetooth and cable only (the 2.4 GHz receiver is a separate RK61 variant).
standout_why: Compared against mkbguide.com and rottenwifi.com (both cited), official.deals under-50, mechvibes.com and keebspicks.net, all opened 2026-11-21. None cites RTINGS or any lab, and none gives a latency, measured battery or noise figure; their numbers are maker or listing specs. mkbguide names the RK61 'Best Wireless' with no battery, weight or latency; mechvibes and keebspicks say outright they have not tested the boards. The finding is new against all five, but it covers one candidate only and RTINGS locks its millisecond values behind membership, so there is no side-by-side table.
decides: It does not pick a winner; it removes one. ChatGPT's second answer calls the RK61 'a well-known budget choice, especially for gaming' and 'tri-mode wireless'; RTINGS' test of the Bluetooth-plus-wired RK61 says the opposite for gaming, and shows why ChatGPT's 'verify the exact revision' matters (the receiver is a separate variant). No named lab measurement was found for ATK A87, Rosewill Neon S75, Redragon K530 Pro, DAREU FLEX75, Redragon K526 Pro, Gamakay TK101 or Gamakay NS68 tri-mode, so the page's pick among those has to rest on maker specs and price from other angles. The page can say plainly that only one board in this price band has a lab test behind it.

findings.label: Effective update rate vs polling rate (RTINGS)
findings.value: 250 Hz effective update rate, bottlenecking a 1,000 Hz polling rate
findings.source_title: ROYAL KLUDGE RK61 Keyboard Review - RTINGS.com
findings.note: RTINGS wording: "a low effective update rate of 250Hz bottlenecks its polling rate of 1000Hz." The direct fetch returned only navigation, so the review text was read through a text reader (r.jina.ai) of the same URL.

findings.label: Latency verdict (RTINGS)
findings.value: "high and inconsistent"; RTINGS lists high latency as a drawback for competitive gaming
findings.source_title: ROYAL KLUDGE RK61 Keyboard Review - RTINGS.com
findings.note: Verdict wording only. The millisecond values (wired, Bluetooth) are locked behind RTINGS membership on the page and are not quoted here.

findings.label: Variant RTINGS tested and its connections
findings.value: Wireless RK61 with blue backlighting and hot-swappable RK Brown switches; connections Bluetooth and wired, no 2.4 GHz receiver. RTINGS lists a separate 'RK61 2.4 GHz' variant with a receiver.
findings.source_title: ROYAL KLUDGE RK61 Keyboard Review - RTINGS.com
findings.note: RTINGS: "We tested the wireless version of the ROYAL KLUDGE RK61 with blue backlighting and hot-swappable RK Brown switches." The measurements apply to that variant; the tri-mode RK61 ChatGPT showed at $48.99 on Newegg may be a different variant.

findings.label: RTINGS test bench and update date
findings.source_title: ROYAL KLUDGE RK61 Keyboard Review - RTINGS.com
findings.note: Changelog also lists test bench 1.4.2 (2026-01-09) and 1.3.1 (2023-11-29). The original publication date is not shown on the page.

findings.label: Cited rival mkbguide.com: measurements carried
findings.value: No lab or named-reviewer measurement; RK61 listed as 'Best Wireless' with Bluetooth 5.0, three devices and 61 keys, and no battery, weight or latency

findings.label: Cited rival rottenwifi.com: measurements carried
findings.value: No latency, battery-hours, weight or noise measurement; RK61 given as $49.99 at the RK store with a 1,450 mAh battery (maker spec)
findings.source_title: 7 Best Mechanical Keyboards Under $50 (2026 Buying Guide)
findings.note: Article dated 2026-10-01 with price snapshots from 2026-08-16; its RK61 price is not a today price. Sources it names are PCWorld, ErrorEmpire, Price.Review and maker pages.

findings.label: Uncited rivals official.deals, mechvibes.com, keebspicks.net: measurements carried
findings.value: None of the three cites RTINGS or any lab; all figures are listing or maker specs
findings.source_title: The 4 best keyboards under $50, by how often people play them - Mechvibes
findings.note: Mechvibes says its authors have not used the boards and ranks by sound-pack plays. keebspicks.net (https://keebspicks.net/best-mechanical-keyboards-under-50/) says its picks come from listings, not hands-on testing. official.deals (https://www.official.deals/best/mechanical-keyboards/under-50) is a deal list built from product titles. All three opened 2026-11-21.

unsourced: RTINGS' millisecond latency values for the RK61 (wired, Bluetooth), plus its weight, typing noise and switch force: the review page locks them behind membership; a search summary quoted figures but I could not open them, so they are left out.
Any RTINGS, Notebookcheck or other lab measurement for ATK A87, Rosewill Neon S75, Redragon K530 Pro, DAREU FLEX75 or Redragon Volcano K526 Pro: an RTINGS search returned no review of any of them.

PC Gamer's Gamakay TK101 review (weight, 4,000 mAh battery, Gamakay's battery-hours rating) and TechRadar's TK101 review (battery drain the reviewer observed): both pages returned only navigation to the fetcher and a reader proxy was refused (HTTP 403), so no figure from either is reported.
Measured latency for the Gamakay x NaughShark NS68 tri-mode on 2.4 GHz or Bluetooth: no lab test found, and PC Gamer's NS68 review body could not be opened to confirm which variant it tested.
RTINGS' own budget mechanical keyboard list, for a lab-tested wireless pick under $50: the URL I tried returned 404.
Today's US store prices for the rival boards: not read in this angle (tool budget went to the measurement pages).
